findings.problem: The card asks whether 'pharmacist administration authority in Massachusetts' is a general licence to administer any prescription injectable, and answers: 'It reaches the medications on the circular's exhaustive list, for a pharmacist or pharmacy intern who meets the conditions attached to it.' The 'No' is right, but the scope it gives for Massachusetts pharmacist administration authority is too narrow, so the answer is wrong as it stands.
findings.rationale: The circular's list is exhaustive for its own pathway, dispensing by administration under its conditions. It does not mark the outer edge of what a Massachusetts pharmacist may administer. The current 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9)(e), which this section itself teaches (orientation[10], comparison_tables[2], decision_logic[0], retrieval_prompts[28]), lets a pharmacist administer controlled substances in an Opioid Treatment Program pursuant to an order. That includes methadone, which is not on the list. The current 105 CMR 700.004(B)(6) separately lets a registered pharmacist or pharmacy intern dispense by administration influenza vaccine, COVID-19 vaccine and other Department-designated immunizations to persons five years of age or older, pursuant to the order of a practitioner, and 105 CMR 700.003(F) adds vaccine administration under a Commissioner's order. A candidate drilling this card by itself would learn that a Massachusetts pharmacist may administer only the listed medications, and could answer an immunization or opioid treatment program item wrongly. Elsewhere the section scopes the same point correctly to 'the pathway' (orientation[0], worked_examples[3].steps[4], common_traps[28]) and flags vaccines as resting on separate authorities (orientation[11], decision_logic[15]). That is why a minor edit is enough: scope the question and answer to the Department's prescription pathway under Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124.

findings.problem: 'Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 lists by generic name the only medications a pharmacist or pharmacy intern may administer' drops the circular's word 'eligible' and the pathway it belongs to. The line reads as a global limit on what a Massachusetts pharmacist or intern may administer.
findings.rationale: The circular's sentence ('are the only medications eligible to be administered by a pharmacist or pharmacy intern') sits under its heading Medications Eligible for Pharmacist or Pharmacy Intern Administration and serves its dispensing-by-administration conditions. 105 CMR 700.004(B)(6), on immunizations, and 700.004(B)(9)(e), on opioid treatment program administration by order, are separate administration authorities. This line tracks the circular's own wording closely and the section's edges paragraph offsets it, so the risk is smaller than in retrieval_prompts[30]. The same scoping edit resolves it, for example 'the only medications eligible under the circular's pathway'.

authorities.exact_section: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Medications Eligible for Pharmacist or Pharmacy Intern Administration, opening sentence

findings.problem: The paragraph first rejects a reading of the NOTE under which 'only' would confine every administration of an addiction-treatment medication to a registered opioid treatment program. It then says 'On either reading the course that is safe is the same', and that safe course includes giving the listed long-acting injectables in a pharmacy on a prescription. Under the broad reading, pharmacy administration of the listed buprenorphine and naltrexone injectables would not be a safe course, so the two readings do not in fact give the same answer.
findings.rationale: The conclusion the section acts on is correct. The circular's Purpose and eligible list expressly authorize pharmacist and pharmacy intern administration of long-acting injectable buprenorphine and naltrexone under its prescription conditions, and the NOTE speaks of administration 'pursuant to an order', so the broad reading cannot stand against the list. The sentence should say that, not claim the same safe course on both readings. No answer on Massachusetts facts changes.

authorities.exact_section: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Purpose; NOTE following Dispensing by Administration; Long-Acting Injectable Medications for Substance Use Disorders

findings.problem: The patient brings 'two valid prescriptions', one 'for methadone for addiction treatment'. Federal rules do not support a valid prescription for that purpose. 21 CFR 1306.04(c) provides for prescriptions for detoxification or maintenance treatment for Schedule III, IV or V controlled substances. Under 21 CFR 1306.07(a), a Schedule II narcotic for maintenance or detoxification treatment may be administered or dispensed directly '(but not prescribe)' by a practitioner separately registered with DEA as a narcotic treatment program.
findings.rationale: The example's conclusion is unaffected: the methadone may not be administered at the pharmacy under either route taught. Federal law is outside the section's declared scope. Still, calling the methadone prescription 'valid' could leave a candidate thinking a community pharmacy could at least fill methadone for opioid use disorder on a prescription. Dropping 'valid' for that document, or adding a one-line federal note, would avoid the implication. Released MA-Q-0329 uses the same premise ('a valid prescription from a practitioner'). Its key is unaffected, and it remains answerable from and consistent with the section.

findings.problem: The role 'Prescriber of an eligible medication' is given the duty to 'Prescribe in single doses, with or without refills'.
findings.rationale: In the circular, single-dose prescribing is condition (d) of a pharmacist's or pharmacy intern's dispensing by administration. It is not a directive to prescribers. The circular's words to prescribers are that they 'must regularly re-assess', 'should' include the notation, are 'strongly encouraged' to communicate, and are 'urged' to issue separate emergency-medication prescriptions. As a prescriber duty the item names the wrong actor. It would be accurate as a statement of what the prescription must say for the pathway to be used. It is unlikely to mislead a pharmacist candidate.

authorities.exact_section: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Dispensing by Administration condition (d); Prescriber Assessment; Pharmacist-Prescriber Communication

findings.problem: The paragraph says that, kept apart, 'each proposition stays with its source', and the section follows the circular in opening all five categories to pharmacy interns. It never draws out two facts. Clause (c) of the definition of Administer names only 'a registered pharmacist'. The regulation's naming of a pharmacy intern in 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9) reaches only FDA approved mental health or substance use disorder treatment drugs. So for testosterone, HIV prevention and sexually transmitted infection medications, an intern's authorization rests on the circular alone.
findings.rationale: This does not mislead on Massachusetts facts. The Department's circular expressly names pharmacy interns in its Purpose, its Dispensing by Administration paragraph and its list heading, the section reports that accurately, and comparison_tables[0] shows the statutory actor as a registered pharmacist. It is a point about which source says what, and it belongs with learning objective 11, next to the section's careful handling of interns on the opioid treatment program route.

results.summary: I checked the section against the current official texts. These were M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1 (Administer, clauses (b) and (c)(i)-(iii)) and s. 9(a); the 105 CMR 700.004(B) heading and (B)(9)(a)-(e) in the current 105 CMR 700.000 PDF generated 2024-02-02; and Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 of 11 March 2026, read in full from the DOCX linked on the mass.gov news page. The statutory, regulatory and guidance propositions are accurate. The three statutory routes and their gates are right, as is the pharmacist's 'as limited by' place on the s. 9(a) list with its possession and administration limbs. So are the regulation's heading, its 18-or-older reach for mental health and substance use disorder drugs, conditions (a)-(d), (d)1. and 6., and the (e) opioid treatment program route. The section also presents the circular as Department guidance and gives each circular duty its own modality: an exhaustive list by generic name; subcutaneous or intramuscular only and not intravenous, per labeling and REMS; single-dose packaging and prescribing with or without refills; training, CPR, competency, emergency competency and counseling as 'must'; the pharmacy's record list; 'should ... within 24 hours' against 'must be immediately reported'; Board reporting 'in accordance with Board regulations'; privacy; and a Pharmacist-Prescriber Communication paragraph written wholly as encouragement. Where the texts leave points open, the safe courses it gives are actually safe: 18 or older for every category, no pharmacy-intern use of the opioid treatment program route, and an event needing emergency medical services reported immediately as the adverse-event section outlines. All seven practice questions (MA-Q-0329, MA-Q-0330, MA-Q-0331, MA-Q-0332, MA-Q-0356, MA-Q-0359, MA-Q-0423) can be answered from the section, and nothing in it contradicts their keys or explanations. One criterion fails, overgeneralization. retrieval_prompts[30] answers that Massachusetts pharmacist administration authority 'reaches the medications on the circular's exhaustive list'. On its own that is wrong, given 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9)(e), which this section teaches, and 700.004(B)(6). quick_review[8] has a milder form of the same breadth. The Low findings concern the 'on either reading' sentence in orientation[10]; the 'valid' methadone-for-addiction prescription in worked_examples[1], measured against 21 CFR 1306.04(c) and 1306.07(a); the prescriber 'duty' to prescribe in single doses in role_duties[3]; and the statute/regulation/guidance layering of a pharmacy intern's authority, which the section never draws out. Scoping the two study items to the Department's prescription pathway would make the section publishable; the Low items are optional polish.
